items.title: UK operation wards off risk of cyber-attack on supermarket fridges and freezers

An attack would have been similar to those that have caused many millions of euros of damage in continental Europe in recent months. But, while many retailers have now been protected, researchers warned that many more could still be vulnerable. Continue reading...

items.title: EU wants ‘closest possible relationship’ with UK after agreeing Brexit reset deal – live
items.desc: President of European Council says EU ‘remains open to have the closest possible relationship’ with the UK Senior correspondent Making today’s reset deal contingent on a further agreement on the level of tuition fees for EU citizens is designed to neutralise the leverage London gets in the next six months, EU sources have said. Senior diplomats had already confirmed this week that the EU would defer the deal on the level of tuition fees for another six months , a move designed to give the UK leverage in parallel negotiations to have the UK included in Made in Europe legislation designed to protect EU supply chains against China. But the move to make the food and drink deal also contingent on a tuition fees deal effectively seeks to neutralise the leverage the UK gets today. items.title: Burnham seals trade and youth mobility deals in biggest step towards EU since Brexit
items.desc: Agreements reached on food and drink, emissions and to allow young people to move around continent, but may be derailed over student fees Andy Burnham has taken the biggest step towards deeper ties with the EU since Brexit, sealing deals to ease trade and create a mobility scheme for young people as he declared a “new world” of cooperation between the two sides. At a major summit in Brussels on Friday the EU and UK announced three deals, on food and drink, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme, which will allow 100,000 young Britons to live, work, study and travel in the EU, with reciprocal access for Europeans in the UK. Continue reading...

items.title: Voters in four out of five UK parliamentary seats back rejoining EU
items.desc: Survey of more than 7,000 shows that people in hundreds of former leave areas now want to rejoin EU Voters in four out of five UK parliamentary seats now back rejoining the EU, including hundreds of former leave areas, such as the prime minister’s constituency of Makerfield, according to polling. The constituency-level modelling across Great Britain found that 512 seats now favoured rejoining, while 73 backed staying out, and 47 were too close to call, in a survey that will boost Andy Burnham’s case for opening the debate on returning to the EU. items.title: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as ‘biggest breakthrough in decades’
items.desc: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades. In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib , during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body. Continue reading...

items.title: Is it time to change the UK age of consent? – podcast
items.desc: After Russell Brand’s conviction and accusations against David Walliams, campaigners are calling for a staggered age of consent. Nosheen Iqbal speaks to the columnist Polly Hudson and the educator Michael Conroy about what needs to change Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com Anger, disgust, shame. In the last couple of weeks, as news of famous older men being convicted and accused of crimes against very young women and girls has emerged, the public mood has shifted. The conversation has moved from “how did society let this happen?” to “how do we stop it from happening again?”. In that space, a campaign has grown for the consent gap to be closed.
